questions.q: A city's population is modeled by $P(t) = 12000(1.035)^t$, where $t$ is in years.
parts: State the initial population and the annual growth rate.
Find the population after 10 years, to the nearest person.
answers: Initial population 12,000; growth rate 3.5% per year.

questions.q: An account earns 4% annual interest compounded continuously. How long does it take an investment to double? Give an exact expression and a decimal to two places.
Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years: $A(t) = A_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/5730}$.
parts: What fraction of the original carbon-14 remains after 2000 years? Answer to three decimal places.
A sample retains 30% of its carbon-14. Estimate its age to the nearest hundred years.

questions.q: A 200 g sample of a radioactive substance decays to 50 g in 12 hours, following $A(t) = 200e^{kt}$.
parts: Find the half-life of the substance.
answers: $200 \to 50$ is two halvings in 12 h, so the half-life is exactly 6 hours (equivalently $\frac{\ln 2}{0.1155} \approx 6.0$ h).

questions.q: Newton's law of cooling: coffee at $90°$C cools in a $20°$C room following $T(t) = 20 + 70e^{-0.1t}$ ($t$ in minutes). Find the temperature after 10 minutes, to one decimal place.
A lake is stocked with fish, and the population is modeled by $P(t) = \frac{5000}{1+9e^{-0.4t}}$, where $t$ is in years.
parts: Find the carrying capacity (the value $P$ approaches as $t\to\infty$).

questions.q: Two towns start with 10,000 people. Town A grows at a constant rate of 300 people/year (linear); Town B grows at 3% per year (exponential). Find each town's population after 15 years, to the nearest person, and state which is larger.

A radioactive isotope decays from 80 g to 10 g over 3 half-lives. Find the half-life in terms of the decay time, and write the exponential decay model $A(t) = 80e^{kt}$, finding $k$ if the total elapsed time is 15 years (4 d.p.).
questions.answer: $80\to10$ over 3 halvings ($80\to40\to20\to10$) means $3$ half-lives $=15$ years, so half-life $=5$ years. Using $A(15)=10$: $10=80e^{15k}$, so $k=\frac{\ln(1/8)}{15}\approx-0.1386$.

questions.q: The fish population model $P(t)=\frac{5000}{1+9e^{-0.4t}}$ (from earlier) is graphed below. Use the graph to estimate where the population is growing fastest, then explain why this happens near the inflection point.
questions.answer: The curve is steepest near its midpoint, roughly where $P\approx2500$ (half the carrying capacity), consistent with the logistic model's fastest growth occurring at $P=\frac{L}{2}$.

questions.q: Derive a general formula for the doubling time $T$ of a quantity growing as $A(t)=A_0e^{kt}$, in terms of $k$.
Using the doubling-time formula derived above, find the doubling time for a population growing at a continuous rate of $k=0.025$ per year, to one decimal place.
Derive a general formula for the half-life $T_{1/2}$ of a quantity decaying as $A(t)=A_0e^{kt}$ (with $k<0$), in terms of $k$.
A radioactive isotope has decay constant $k=-0.023$ per year. Use the formula above to find its half-life, to one decimal place.
A savings account earns continuous interest, growing from 5000 to 5512.50 riyals in 2 years. Find the annual interest rate $r$ using $A=Pe^{rt}$, to two decimal places (as a percentage).
